components.name: Live Path
components.description: Signature motion: a gradient pulse travelling a purple hairline between nodes; static under reduced motion.
components.css: .ds-path { position: relative; display: flex; justify-content: space-between; padding: 12px 0; } .ds-path::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 8%; right: 8%; top: 50%; height: 1px; background: rgb(168 123 255 / 0.5); opacity: 0.6; } .ds-path-node { position: relative; z-index: 1; padding: 10px 16px; border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / 0.14); border-radius: 6px; background: #121217; color: #ededef; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 500; } .ds-path-pulse { position: absolute; top: 50%; left: 8%; width: 36px; height: 2px; margin-top: -1px; border-radius: 2px; background: linear-gradient(90deg, transparent, #a87bff); animation: ds-travel 4.8s cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.55, 1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-travel { 0% { left: 8%; opacity: 0; } 8% { opacity: 1; } 88% { opacity: 1; } 100% { left: calc(92% - 36px); opacity: 0; } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-path-pulse { display: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Kaisora's world is a dark developer-tool console: a near-black ground, charcoal panels drawn with 1px hairlines, an off-white grotesk, and one dark purple signal. Nothing is claimed that can't be shown; the brand's evidence is a real production architecture rendered as a live diagram, with requests visibly travelling through it. Every other surface (service cards, the featured project, case studies, the founder block) is built from the same panel-and-hairline material so the whole site reads as one instrument.

Density is calm and precise rather than packed. Sections are separated by generous vertical space (112px margin plus 96px padding over a single top hairline), panels carry their content with modest internal padding, and type is tight-tracked and heavy only at the top of the hierarchy. Dark is the home theme; light mode is the same system inverted through the same tokens, not a separate design.

The accent is rare and functional. Purple fills the one primary action per region and marks things that are live: path lines, pulses, junction dots, status text, step counters. Mono type appears only where the content is genuinely system data.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground, charcoal panels, 1px translucent-white hairlines in three strengths.
One accent in two forms: a deep purple fill for primary actions and a light purple tint for live lines, dots and accent text.
Rethink Sans for every voice; Geist Mono only for real system data.
Flat surfaces separated by hairlines; one soft ambient shadow reserved for the live system panel.
Motion that represents work (pulses, an event feed), and stops entirely under reduced motion.
Dark default, light as an inversion, switched by `data-theme` on `<html>`.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Purple is the only hue in the system. It marks a primary action or something live; it never decorates a heading, a background field or a body paragraph.

rules.name: The Fill and Tint Rule
rules.body: The deep purple is a fill (with white text); the light tint is a line, a dot or a short run of text. Never set tint text on a purple fill, and never use the deep purple as text on the dark ground.

rules.name: The Inverted Twin Rule
rules.body: Light mode is not designed separately. Any new token gets a value in both `html[data-theme]` blocks, or it does not ship.

rules.name: The Real Data Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for content a system would actually emit: service names and roles, environments, events, technology tags, ordinal counters. It is never used for section labels, decoration or "techy" flavour.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: Headings stand alone. No eyebrow or kicker line above a title; provenance (project type, role) goes beneath the title in accent text.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Containers are separated by 1px translucent borders and tonal steps. If a new card needs a shadow to read as a card, its border or tone is wrong.

dos: **Do** fill exactly one primary action per region with Signal Purple and white text; everything else is ghost or text.
**Do** build every new container from Panel, a 1px `hairline-2` border and the 6px or 8px radius.
**Do** use the tint for live states, connectors and short accent text, and Signal Purple for that text in light mode.
**Do** set system data (service names, environments, events, tags, counters) in Geist Mono, and everything else in Rethink Sans.
**Do** open each section with a top hairline and the 112px/96px rhythm.
**Do** give every looping animation a resting state and stop it under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** define every new colour token in both theme blocks.
donts: **Don't** introduce a second accent hue; the comp's aqua was replaced by purple and must not return.
**Don't** put an eyebrow or kicker above a heading.
**Don't** use mono for labels, headings or decoration.
**Don't** apply gradients to text, or use purple as a large background field; glows stay soft halos behind content.
**Don't** add shadows to cards; the panel-lift shadow belongs to the live system panel alone.
**Don't** fill sections with icon grids; icons are single-colour line glyphs inside nodes, services and buttons.
